title: CTAs- Innovation Meets Legacy & the BlackRock Effect - Systematic Investor 329

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/CTAs- Innovation Meets Legacy & the BlackRock Effect - Systematic Investor 329.docx

speakers: Tom Roble (Societe Generale Prime Services, CTA indices)
summary:
Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor 329 (Jan 2025): SG CTA indices, replication-based managed futures versus real CTAs, AUM trends, BlackRock's ETF filing, bonds' failure as diversifier.
Conclusions: replication gives cheap, noisy exposure with a compounding cost edge; trend is commoditized; bonds failing and information framing drive diversifier demand.

completeness_estimate: 0.87 - speaker attribution in the unlabelled captions is right except one claim (C21-2); first reader caught all main arguments but missed a few caveats (fee data, index evolution counterpoint, replicability limits, stated vs revealed demand).

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the Trump Administration is bringing back a sense of animal spirits back into the US
claims.claim: Andrew expects the new US administration, staffed by self-made billionaires focused on where America can go over the next 20 years, to revive animal spirits in the US.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: after 100 basis points cut by the FED that you know long-term rates have really moved up and it hasn't been a great year for fixed income
claims.claim: In 2024 long-term rates rose after 100bp of Fed cuts and long-maturity bonds (TLT about -8%) lost, undermining bonds as the 60/40 protection and strengthening the case for trend following.
claims.indicator: TLT 2024 return, long-term yields after Fed cuts

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: with the CBOE skew index uh hitting a new alltime high in December
claims.claim: The CBOE SKEW index at an all-time high in December 2024 means investors are paying for crash protection, so many may be worried about a market decline.
claims.testable: yes - SKEW vs forward equity returns

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: what happens is when when people have a favorite asset class which Bonds were for 20 years and it starts to do badly everybody's first instinct is how do you defend it
claims.claim: Allocators with no playbook for failing bonds keep hoping for recovery (2023 and 2024 were both billed the year of the bond), delaying a shift of capital into diversifiers such as managed futures.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: bonds have done nothing zero sharp ratio over that period of time
claims.claim: In the first five years of the 2020s bonds produced a zero Sharpe ratio, a key trigger for growing managed futures since the old argument was just to hold bonds.
claims.testable: yes - compute bond Sharpe over the period

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: maybe at 6040 moving to 60220 um maybe that's where you take more of the money from
claims.claim: Rather than moving 60/40 to 50/30/20, allocators may move to 60/20/20 by taking the diversifier money from bonds while keeping equities.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the average 12month return after um a great two calendar year uh performance like we've just seen is not very impressive it's pretty flat actually
claims.claim: After a very strong two calendar years for the S&P 500 (best since 1988) the average next 12-month return has historically been flat, so allocators may worry equities will not keep growing.
claims.indicator: S&P 500 two-year return then next 12-month return

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: sock gen Trend up 1.4% in December up 2.56% for the year
claims.claim: In 2024 CTA indices were modest (SG CTA +2.24%, SG Trend +2.56%, BTOP50 +4.44%) versus S&P 500 +25.2%, MSCI World +17.7% and US Aggregate Bond +1.82%.
claims.indicator: SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-Term, BTOP50, Bridge Alternatives index, S&P 500

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: 2024 was an interesting period in q1 and then a really difficult period through Q2 and Q3 of coming back with stronger performance in Q4
claims.claim: Trend following in 2024 was good in Q1, hard in Q2 and Q3 and strong again in Q4.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: it includes Trend following and non Trend following strategies and approximately half the constituents so the top 20 half of those are non- Trend
claims.claim: The SG CTA Index holds the 20 largest open CTAs, about half non-trend (quant macro, short-term under 10 days hold, commodity-only, technical), while SG Trend and short-term indices are subsets, and CTA is a regulatory term not a synonym for trend following.
claims.indicator: SG CTA Index (top 20), SG Trend (top 10), SG Short-Term Traders

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: we tend to see a lot of performance dispersion in the short-term space and so often the groups struggle to persist with performance for many years in a row
claims.claim: Short-term CTAs show high performance dispersion and rarely persist for many years, making asset raising difficult and index turnover highest there, while SG CTA and SG Trend had no constituent changes for 2025.
claims.testable: yes - persistence of short-term CTA rankings

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: a hedge fund index has limited applicability outside of that $300 billion of institutional investors and family offices that invest directly in hedge funds because in the wealth management space most people cannot invest in hedge funds
claims.claim: Hedge fund indices are only usable by institutions that can invest in hedge funds, so wealth managers need an investable, mechanical approximation, which motivated replication.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: over a onewe interval over a very very shortterm period on Monday afternoon we can we can estimate the broad Factor exposures so using only 10 Deep liquid markets
claims.claim: Replication: each Monday regress the index's recent reported returns on about 10 deep liquid markets (S&P 500, 10y Treasury, etc.) to estimate factor exposures accurate enough that next week's return is close to the index, a mechanical method unchanged since 2015-16.
claims.indicator: factor decomposition of SG CTA index on 10 liquid futures, weekly

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: some sort of an estimate of the pree pre-trading cost returns aim for that and then see how we do over the course of next week
claims.claim: The replicator targets pre-trading-cost index returns because fees paid vary across investors, then compares itself to that over the next week.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: over the course of a year you might outperform 80% of the time the index over the course of three years you get into the 90s
claims.claim: A low-cost replicator beats the noisy index only about 53-54% of weeks (monthly tracking error about 60bp), but the small edge from lower fees compounds to about 80% of years and 90% of three-year periods.
claims.indicator: rolling outperformance frequency of replicator vs SG CTA index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's statistically Incredibly Close to the sock gen CT index with 20 managers
claims.claim: A five-manager flat-fee index (Bridge Alternatives) tracks the 20-manager SG CTA Index very closely, so diversification arrives quickly with 2-4 managers and lifts index correlation to the 80s percent.
claims.indicator: Bridge Alternatives Index vs SG CTA Index

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: an average fee in the SG CTA index of 1.3% management fee and 13.9% performance fee
claims.claim: The SG CTA Index constituents average a 1.3% management and 13.9% performance fee; SG Trend average 1.1% and 11%.
claims.indicator: average fees SG CTA / SG Trend

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the performance of the SG Trend index is marginally better over that 9-year period and the bridge alternative has produced 50% higher draw Downs
claims.claim: Over nine years the low flat-fee Bridge Alternatives index did not beat the SG Trend index and had 50% larger drawdowns, so low fees alone did not deliver better performance.
claims.indicator: Bridge Alternatives Index vs SG Trend Index returns and drawdowns

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: the draw down and the often the risk that we are taking is very very different from the real life ctas that we see in the in the SG Trend or the SG CTA index
claims.claim: A bottom-up trend tracker may match long-term return and correlation but its drawdowns and risk differ from real CTAs, because it omits individual markets and risk management.
claims.indicator: SG trend indicator tracker vs real CTAs

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: what are people looking for when they're investing in this space generally they're looking for low correlation to stocks and bonds you know low beted equities Alpha generation performance
claims.claim: Investors seek low correlation to stocks and bonds, low equity beta, alpha and crisis performance; replication aims to retain these properties.
claims.indicator: correlation to stocks and bonds, crisis alpha

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when you limit the factor set you're kind of in the0 8ish range um and you tend to have the same beta same correlation uh and and say crisis Alpha
claims.claim: Replication with a full factor set correlates around 0.9 to the index and about 0.8 with a limited set, with similar equity beta and crisis alpha.
claims.indicator: correlation of replicator to SG CTA Index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: a market environment that was very anti-trend between the fed putut and everything else you had cash earning zero
claims.claim: The late-2010s Long Winter (anti-trend markets from the Fed put, zero cash return, high fees) produced zero net returns for years.
claims.conditions: when cash earns zero and markets mean-revert

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you can capture those same statistical benefits but with 10 or 20 basis points a year of trading costs with a handful of instruments
claims.claim: Replication can capture the same statistical benefits with 10-20bp of trading costs; the SG CTA index beats cash in about 60% of rolling 1-year periods, rising to 80%+ once costs and expenses are eliminated.
claims.indicator: rolling 1-year excess over cash, trading cost

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: as your portfolio expands and as the liquidity of those positions goes down it is natural for firms to limit the sizes of those positions
claims.claim: Large CTAs cap sizes in illiquid idiosyncratic markets, so single markets like cocoa contribute little to their results.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: about five or six million billion dollars that was being made in Coco over about a two or three month period
claims.claim: Cocoa's roughly $5-6bn profit over 2-3 months is small relative to $300bn of CTA assets, so missing cocoa matters little for a replicator.
claims.indicator: cocoa profit estimate $5-6bn vs CTA AUM $300bn

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there are periods where replication will underperform but it's because there are multiple things that are working at the same time
claims.claim: Replication underperforms when many markets it does not hold (Mexican peso, Canadian rates, softs, commodities) trend at once, but idiosyncratic hits and misses mostly cancel across managers.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: Commodities is that standout sector which was contributing I would say for most of the trend followers a large part of their p&l
claims.claim: In 2024 commodities were the standout P&L sector for trend followers, with the top commodity markets in the trend indicator contributing much of the theoretical portfolio P&L.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: but if oil is moving in a big way it's probably pulling other markets along with it so it's not that we're going to get zero exposure to Commodities
claims.claim: Because large commodity moves pull other markets, a replicator holding oil and gold still captures some exposure to markets it does not trade (planets and moons).

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you tend to take a lot more risk you tend to have much higher draw Downs
claims.claim: Concentrating on idiosyncratic high-asymmetry bets raises risk and drawdowns and is hard to model ex ante, so broad factor exposure is more reliable.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: most allocators that I know well who invest with us combine us with other funs precisely because they recognize that we're very open about the things we're not doing
claims.claim: Replication is an incremental tool and allocators combine it with managers like Man AHL, who are better at short-term inflections.
claims.indicator: blend of replicator and single managers

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: diversification is the only free lunch Standalone a market maybe has a trend following sharp ratio of 0.2.3 but if you add more and more assets together you can increase that shock ratio
claims.claim: Trend Sharpe of a single market (0.2-0.3) rises with more markets, and many CTAs reach roughly 0.9 only by adding many idiosyncratic bets, which a 10-instrument replicator cannot access.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I don't think it's an economic decision on their part um I think it's I think it's a client communication issue
claims.claim: Investors blend replication with short-term-capable managers for client communication rather than economics, because after an event such as SVB they want to say they hold someone responsive.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we're going to underperform by few maybe several hundred basis points after the inflection point the reason we don't try to model around it is because half the time the guys with short-term models in it's actually a head fake
claims.claim: A weekly replicator lags at sharp inflections (SVB) by several hundred bp but catches up within months, since half of inflections are head fakes that wrong-foot short-term models.
claims.indicator: replicator lag after sharp inflection (SVB March 2023)

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the general idea is it's supposed to be predictable and predictable means consistent
claims.claim: An index should be predictable and unchanged over time; replication's index-like ethos suits wealth managers who want a consistent product.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: what matters is finding a great diversifier that he can put into a portfolio that he doesn't otherwise have access to in in a in a reasonable predictable way
claims.claim: ETF model-portfolio managers care about an accessible, predictable diversifier rather than which commodity is ripping.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: and I can see what would this have made my life better over the past 25 years
claims.claim: Index products win in wealth management because investors can evaluate 20-25 years of history and are never wrong versus a benchmark.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I think where we as managers uh are consistently or constantly learning things is probably a little bit on the risk management side
claims.claim: Trend followers make only small tweaks to models (few ways to do trend following); improvement over the last decade is mainly in risk management and execution.
claims.indicator: trend model changes vs risk management

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: 25% of the managers in the sgct index do not include interest income
claims.claim: About 25% of SG CTA index managers exclude interest income, so index returns understate those of funds including it, a bias when comparing with replicators.
claims.indicator: interest income inclusion in SG CTA Index

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: don't think ctas are developing new trend following models Trends are pretty easy to recognize
claims.claim: Trend models are standard off-the-shelf (e.g. moving-average crossover); the edge lies in implementation, risk allocation and recognition of over-extended trends, with risk management and execution the main innovation areas.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: it's been fairly stable since then I think it's bounced as you say between 300 and 350 post 2014
claims.claim: Managed futures AUM grew to about $350bn in 2009-10 and has stayed between $300bn and $400bn since, with the main increase after strong 2022 performance.

correction.issue: Range misstated: Tom says AUM has bounced between $300bn and $350bn since 2014 (the $350-400bn range is Niels's Barclay Hedge recollection).
correction.fix: Managed futures AUM grew to about $350bn in 2009-10 and, per Tom, has stayed between about $300bn and $350bn since 2014 (Niels recalls $350-400bn from Barclay Hedge), with the main increase after strong 2022 performance.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: back in 2010 to be in the index you had to be approximately 800 million that then grew to 1 billion in 2016
claims.claim: The size cutoff for the SG CTA Index rose from $800m (2010) to $1bn (2016), $1.5bn (2019) and $1.82bn now, with growth in the mid-sized group, while the SG Trend (top 10) minimum is $4.8bn.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: almost 90% of new start Quant what we would call a CTA is
claims.claim: Trend following is about 80% of the CTA space and commoditized with few entrants; nearly 90% of new quant start-ups are not trend and many are becoming multi-asset quant groups targeting high Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: instead what it happens is it seems to have settled into there's this kind of core Trend which is going to a little bit cheaper it's going to be a little bit more commoditized
claims.claim: The CTA industry has settled into a cheaper, more commoditized core trend with more focus on risk controls and other differentiators, instead of the change Andrew expected in 2015.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I'm much more comfortable making a onewe bet in an industry that I think will change over time then I am making then I am locking myself into a particular way of doing Trend
claims.claim: A one-week replication bet on industry positioning is preferred to locking into a fixed trend design for 10 years, because the industry will evolve.
claims.indicator: top-down replication vs bottom-up fixed model

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: one of the most valuable things they can put in their portfolio is locked at a 50 basis point allocation
claims.claim: Managed futures sits in the hedge fund bucket (a pension has about 8% in hedge funds, of which little in managed futures), so a diversifier with strong statistics gets only about a 50bp allocation, limiting growth.
claims.indicator: managed futures share of hedge fund allocation

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: over lay the CTA or the the Alternatives allocation on top of their Equity portfolio
claims.claim: Portable alpha, overlaying CTAs on top of equity exposure (60/40/20), is rising because margin-based strategies are cheap to implement.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: either they have too much correlation to equities because they are partic participating in equity Trends or they've underperformed but been very non-correlated
claims.claim: CTAs are criticised either for equity correlation or for lagging equities while uncorrelated; investors' expectations misalign with the diversifier objective, e.g. CTAs +2% vs equities +25% in 2024.
claims.indicator: CTA correlation to equities vs relative return

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the ethos of trend following was well we look at prices and we extrapolate from it and and that doesn't fit into their model of we want somebody who's going to show us how they have an information Advantage
claims.claim: Allocators historically want managers with a stock-picking or information-advantage story, so a price-extrapolation strategy fits poorly into their model.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the reason you analyze prices is to essentially extract information in in the markets
claims.claim: Reframing: prices change because information changes, so CTAs pick up information shifts (e.g. inflation 2021) quickly, valuable at inflection points because institutional allocators are slow by design.
claims.testable: partly - narrative with academic support on slow information adoption

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: what hurt the space I think was the whipsaws in sentiment
claims.claim: In 2024 CTAs got the information changes right (long equities early, rates higher for longer) but were hurt by sentiment whipsaws where beliefs flipped back and forth over months.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: this space is trading against every slow moving investor out there
claims.claim: CTA alpha is not zero-sum among managers but earned against slow-moving investors, so managed futures is a completion strategy for a multi-asset portfolio, deserving about 3% not 20% and shining when other assets fall (2022).

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it doesn't go from zero to five it goes from zero to 100 to 500 because you get trillions and trillions of dollars of pools of capital start to move in that direction
claims.claim: Once an asset becomes a strategic allocation (private credit, private equity) flows scale enormously; BlackRock entering managed futures ETFs (US ETF universe $12tn vs managed futures about $2.5bn) could validate and grow the space.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they also control the software called Aladdin that Mo many wealth managers use to determine their own asset allocation models
claims.claim: BlackRock's Aladdin and model portfolios could set managed futures as a 2-3% allocation across wealth management, driving institutional adoption.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: because you're only making these short onewe bets it's actually not that sensitive to what what instruments you use because you're essentially making a short-term correlation bet on the market
claims.claim: Replication barely depends on which instruments are used since it is a short-term correlation bet; the UCITS-friendly version excluding commodities has a nine-year track record.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we add uh the Australian dollar and Canadian dollar so we're in currency land proxies
claims.claim: A non-commodity replication index uses AUD and CAD as proxies for commodities; it should outperform the hedge fund index by about 250-300bp versus 350bp for the standard model, and correlation falls from 0.9 to 0.8.
claims.indicator: AUD and CAD as commodity proxies

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: around a quarter of European investors are looking for things that are ESG sensitive
claims.claim: About a quarter of European investors want ESG-sensitive products and many cannot hold commodities, creating demand for non-commodity CTA exposure.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker: Andrew Beer says this, citing an SG investor survey by Tom ('Tom in his investor survey ... came out a couple of months ago'); Tom does not state it himself.
correction.fix: Andrew Beer, citing Tom's SG investor survey: about a quarter of European investors want ESG-sensitive products and many cannot hold commodities, creating demand for non-commodity CTA exposure.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when you start kicking out asset classes in a traditional Trend fing model you really do lose something
claims.claim: Excluding asset classes from a traditional trend model reduces diversification and returns, which is why replication is attractive for commodity-restricted investors.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: Futures being a zero some game for every long there is a short that offsets it
claims.claim: Futures are zero-sum so ESG labelling of derivatives is unclear; there is no CTA with an SFDR Article 8/9 stamp.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there were two sectors where the average performance uh for each market was positive throughout all the different rolling time period right one was grains the other one was softs
claims.claim: In Niels's program, grains and softs had positive average market performance over every rolling window from 1 to 18 years, supporting commodities as useful in a CTA portfolio.
claims.indicator: rolling average market contribution by sector

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: Germany they just you can't do with agricultural Commodities because they don't want you buing on food stuffs but they're fine with gold oil and everything else
claims.claim: Investor constraints differ by country (German investors avoid agricultural commodities but accept gold and oil), so a single compliant product is hard.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: they are looking more and more to Alternative strategies to fill maybe the void left by bonds
claims.claim: US allocators building 'robust' portfolios increasingly use uncorrelated alternative strategies to fill the diversification gap left by bonds, driven by worry that equity returns will slow.
claims.direction: flows toward diversifiers, away from bonds
claims.conditions: while bonds fail to diversify equities

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if you're a big allocator and you can compress people on fees you'll tend to structurally outperform as well
claims.claim: Large institutional CTA allocators structurally beat the index partly by negotiating lower fees than the headline fees embedded in index returns, the same fee edge replication exploits.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: that's before somebody else's fees on that maybe it's in other words there may be implementation fees that we don't see when you're looking at those numbers
claims.claim: Index return comparisons (e.g. the Bridge Alternatives managed-account index) may exclude implementation or platform fees and need minimums, so their returns overstate what an investor actually gets.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: you're tracking an e an evolving portfolio you're not tracking a portfolio which is a static portfolio every year we change the constituents
claims.claim: Tom challenges the 'unchanging index' claim: a replicator's principal-component weights shift and it tracks an index whose constituents and their models change yearly, so its implementation evolves much like a CTA's research process.
claims.testable: partly - track replicator factor weights over time

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: absolutely not those guys are agreable there's sharp ratios of 2.2 or whatever um no look the thing about replication is you have to know what you can replicate
claims.claim: Multi-strategy pod shops with Sharpe ratios around 2 cannot be replicated, because replication works only where returns come from a few liquid factor exposures, as with trend CTAs.
claims.conditions: replicable only when returns load on liquid factors
claims.testable: yes - out-of-sample factor-replication R2 by strategy type

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's not that people can't see the benefits it's they feel it shouldn't work because past prices are not supposed to be indicative of future performance
claims.claim: Allocators under-allocate to trend following not because they miss the statistical benefits but because they believe past prices should not predict returns (efficient-market prior), so the strategy lacks a credible story for them.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: the way the regory to is interpretated is there shouldn't be any exposure to Commodities
claims.claim: UCITS/ESMA rules are commonly read as banning direct commodity exposure, splitting European investors between dropping commodities from CTA products and adding them back through bank structured notes.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you're not going to find out what they really think until you're standing in front of them
claims.claim: Stated investor demand (e.g. everyone wants a top CTA in an Article 9 wrapper) is unreliable; real demand shows only when a concrete investable product is offered.
